gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ a million euros, I would travel the world for a year.
gaps.explanation: Second conditionals use the past simple after 'if' for unreal presents: won.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ you at the airport last week, but I was abroad.
gaps.hint: regret about a missed past meeting
gaps.explanation: Regret about something that did not happen takes 'wish' plus the past perfect: had met.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ here now, she would know exactly what to do.
gaps.hint: unreal present needs the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: For unreal present conditions, formal English uses 'were' for all persons: were.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: You cannot enter the studio unless you ___ a visitor badge.
gaps.explanation: Rules with 'unless' keep the present simple: wear.

gaps.sentence: In your position, I ___ for a written contract.
gaps.explanation: Giving imaginary advice uses 'would' for an unreal present: would ask.
